title: Adresse à la nation du Président de la République, Félix Tshisekedi suite à la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire à l’est du pays
claim: In his national address, Tshisekedi said he was choosing diplomacy over war, cited the East African Community and Luanda processes, and described the eastern crisis as having displaced more than 200,000 people.
source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement with explicit crisis-management choices and dates.
ruler_attribution: Directly Tshisekedi's own crisis framing and choice set.
contrary_evidence: This concerns conventional-security de-escalation, not nuclear command or arsenal decisions.

title: DRC: One year on, 'State of Siege' used as a tool to crush dissent
claim: Amnesty said the state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri had been used to crush dissent, with two activists killed by security forces, dozens arbitrarily detained, and military courts used against critics.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights briefing with direct reporting and interview-based findings.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Tshisekedi because he maintained the state of siege and was urged to lift its restrictions.
contrary_evidence: The same briefing notes the government said the measure aimed to protect civilians and combat armed groups.

title: 2023 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
publisher: USDOS - U.S. Department of State (via ecoi.net)
claim: The report says 2022 in the DRC featured arbitrary killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary arrest or detention, political prisoners, serious media restrictions, substantial interference with peaceful assembly under the state of siege, serious government corruption, gender-based violence, and ethnic violence; it also says the government took some steps to investigate and punish officials.
source_confidence_reason: Official U.S. human-rights report reproduced by ecoi.net with direct country-specific findings.
ruler_attribution: State-level conduct during Tshisekedi's tenure; not all abuses are proven personal orders.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some government investigative and punitive steps.

title: 2023 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
publisher: USDOS - U.S. Department of State (via ecoi.net)
claim: On August 30 in Goma, government security forces used deadly and disproportionate force against a banned protest, reportedly killing 56 demonstrators and arresting 158 people, after which the governor of North Kivu was relieved of his post and an investigation was launched.
source_confidence_reason: Official U.S. report gives a specific incident, casualty count, and immediate state response.
ruler_attribution: Security forces acted under Tshisekedi's government; the report documents the state response but not a personal order.
contrary_evidence: The report notes a government investigation and some removals/arrests after the incident.

title: 2023 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
publisher: USDOS - U.S. Department of State (via ecoi.net)
claim: The report says police in Maniema arbitrarily arrested three human-rights defenders for protesting mistreatment of the ethnic Twa community, and the chief prosecutor later released them for lack of evidence.
source_confidence_reason: Official report with a named incident, date window, and outcome.
period_fit: Late-2022 / early-2023 follow-through on 2022 repression patterns
ruler_attribution: Relevant to the administration's handling of protest and vulnerable-group defense, though the incident is provincial.
contrary_evidence: The later release indicates some remedy, albeit after arbitrary arrest.

title: 2023 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
publisher: USDOS - U.S. Department of State (via ecoi.net)
claim: The report says political prisoners and detainees were mostly people arrested under defamation laws for criticizing officials or during protests, and that Jean-Marc Kabund remained jailed despite a court order for house arrest.
source_confidence_reason: Official report with direct detail on political detention and due-process failure.
ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Tshisekedi-era detention practice and political-space restrictions.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some prisoners had international-access monitoring.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
claim: Freedom House reports that violent protests against MONUSCO in July 2022 killed 36 people nationwide, that opposition leader Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested in August for allegedly insulting President Tshisekedi, and that assembly rights were curtailed in state-of-siege areas.
source_confidence_reason: Independent country report with specific 2022 incidents and institutional analysis.
period_fit: Direct 2022 developments summarized in a 2023 report
ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's domestic-security and protest-response record.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some opposition figures were released and some exiles returned under Tshisekedi.

title: UNHCR deeply concerned by renewed violence displacing thousands in North Kivu, DR Congo
claim: UNHCR said at least 170,000 civilians had been displaced since the November 2021 escalation, and warned that women and girls faced sexual violence, extortion, and repeated displacement.
source_confidence_reason: Authoritative humanitarian briefing with concrete displacement and protection figures.
ruler_attribution: Indirect state-protection context under Tshisekedi's government.
contrary_evidence: The source describes harm from armed clashes rather than a direct presidential order.

title: In eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the surge in violence has driven thousands of displaced people to the outskirts of Goma
claim: The ICRC said fighting in Rutshuru forced more than 72,000 people to flee in one week and urged all combatants to protect civilians and allow humanitarian workers to reach them.
source_confidence_reason: Primary humanitarian field release with exact displacement figures and civilian-protection appeal.
ruler_attribution: Relevant to the government's civilian-protection responsibilities under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The release does not assign each abuse to the president personally.

title: Les enfants sous attaque dans l'escalade du conflit à l'est de la RDC
claim: UNICEF said armed attacks in Rutshuru killed four children, more than 158,000 people had been displaced since late March, and 652 children were separated from their parents or guardians.
source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF country-office release with concrete child-protection figures.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Tshisekedi's responsibility to protect vulnerable groups.
contrary_evidence: The release describes armed clashes rather than a direct presidential order.

title: DR Congo: Resurgent M23 Rebels Target Civilians
claim: Human Rights Watch said M23 summarily killed at least 29 civilians since mid-June 2022 and that the fighting forced nearly 200,000 people to flee their homes.
source_confidence_reason: Well-documented independent rights report based on interviews and field reporting.
ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to Tshisekedi's protection record and failure-to-prevent context.
contrary_evidence: The killings were attributed to M23, not to Tshisekedi's direct orders.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo
publisher: Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict
claim: The DRC profile recorded 305 children killed or maimed, 557 children victims of sexual violence, and 1,192 children abducted in the year, and said violations by government forces increased, especially killings, maiming, and attacks on schools and hospitals, while some commanders signed child-protection commitments and 430 children were released.
source_confidence_reason: Official UN monitoring page with country-specific 2022 grave-violations statistics and government-related findings.
ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's responsibility for state-force conduct and child protection.
contrary_evidence: The page also reports some government commitments and releases, so the record is mixed rather than uniformly negative.

title: Congo arrests opposition leader Kabund
claim: Reuters reported that opposition leader Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested after a controversy over remarks about President Tshisekedi, and that his lawyers said he was accused of contempt of the head of state.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a politically sensitive arrest.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Tshisekedi-era treatment of a former ally turned opposition figure.
contrary_evidence: The article reports allegations and charges, not a final adjudication of guilt.

title: Journalists targeted by fighters in eastern DRC's Nord-Kivu province
claim: RSF said both government forces and M23 rebels were targeting journalists in North Kivu, that a community radio station had been ransacked after the Bunagana attack, and that journalists were facing threats and cyber-harassment.
locator: article body and quoted RSF Africa-desk statement
source_confidence_reason: Independent press-freedom monitor with direct country-specific reporting.
ruler_attribution: Relevant to the administration's failure to protect journalists, though abuses were perpetrated by multiple actors.
contrary_evidence: The report also assigns some threats to M23 and other armed actors, not only the government.

title: DRC: One year on, 'State of Siege' used as a tool to crush dissent
claim: Amnesty reported that the state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri was being used to crush dissent, with two activists killed by security forces and dozens of critics arbitrarily detained on trumped-up charges.
locator: paragraph beginning 'A State of Siege...' / lines 64-67
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous NGO briefing with named cases, interviews, and direct discussion of the emergency regime.
period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target period; it describes a measure imposed in 2021 and still active in 2022.
ruler_attribution: Tshisekedi directly declared and extended the state of siege; the specific abuses are security-force conduct under a regime he kept in place and tolerated after notice.
contrary_evidence: The government said the state of siege aimed to protect civilians from armed groups.
Armed-group violence also continued in the affected provinces.

title: DRC: Stop using prolonged state of siege as excuse to crush protests
claim: Amnesty said that demanding accountability from DRC authorities in the two eastern provinces had become particularly risky under the prolonged state of siege, with dozens of critics arbitrarily detained and sometimes prosecuted by military courts, while authorities threatened to crush new protests.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous advocacy report focused on protests, detention, and emergency-rule abuse, with direct quotations from Amnesty.
period_fit: Directly in 2022, after more than a year of the state of siege.
ruler_attribution: Attribution is strong for the emergency regime because Tshisekedi kept the state of siege in force; the arrests are carried out by military authorities operating under that regime.
contrary_evidence: The protests were also directed at MONUSCO and the M23 crisis, so not all security pressure originated from the presidency.
The government framed the measure as necessary for security.

title: World Report 2022: Democratic Republic of Congo
claim: HRW reported that in April 2022 police killed five people and wounded at least eight others during peaceful protests in Goma, Butembo, and Beni territory, and that security forces and violent mobs later killed at least 10 people in Nyiragongo territory.
source_confidence_reason: Major rights-monitor synthesis with concrete casualty figures and a clear description of the protest crackdown.
period_fit: The incidents occurred in 2022 and are squarely within the target period.
ruler_attribution: Attribution is partial but meaningful: the killings were by police and security forces under a president who controlled the national security chain and maintained the emergency environment.
contrary_evidence: Some violence was also carried out by violent mobs and not solely by state forces.
The protests were connected to local security tensions, not only presidential policy.

title: World Report 2022: Democratic Republic of Congo
claim: HRW reported that Tshisekedi later apologized to children involved in a police round-up, but only after he appointed the police commander responsible for the round-up, François Kabeya, as mayor of Goma.
source_confidence_reason: Specific attribution to a presidential appointment and a contemporaneous response to abuse, captured in a major rights report.
period_fit: 2022 target period; the appointment and apology are both discussed in the 2022 report.
ruler_attribution: Direct for the appointment, which weakens the remedial value of the apology and suggests tolerance of abusive policing rather than accountability.
contrary_evidence: The president did apologize to the affected children.
The underlying police action was carried out by local security personnel, not by the president personally.

title: Three journalists tortured by DRC intelligence agency
claim: RSF reported that the National Intelligence Agency detained and tortured three journalists in Boende on 18 May 2022 and said that at least ten journalists had been arrested or threatened by the agency since the start of the year.
source_confidence_reason: Detailed contemporaneous press-freedom report with named victims, dates, and the agency involved.
ruler_attribution: The ANR is a state security agency; the evidence supports a strong state nexus and tolerated abuse, though it does not show a personal presidential order for the torture.
contrary_evidence: RSF notes the abuse by the local ANR director rather than a directly documented presidential instruction.
The government could still have ordered an investigation, but the report says the abuse reflected close control and intimidation.

title: Journalists targeted by fighters in eastern DRC’s Nord-Kivu province
claim: RSF said journalists in North Kivu were facing cyber-harassment and frequent death threats from Congolese government supporters, and urged the government to protect journalists and prosecute attackers.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous regional press-freedom monitor with named journalists and a direct warning to the government.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: the threats came from government supporters and reflect a tolerated intimidation climate under the ruling network.
contrary_evidence: Some threats also came from M23-side actors, so the environment was not exclusively state-driven.
This source does not prove a direct presidential order.

title: Freelance reporter abducted, held incommunicado in DRC
claim: RSF reported that freelance reporter Steve Wembi was taken in an abduction-style arrest on 24 October 2022 and remained unlocated, while the government spokesman denied that the ANR was holding him.
source_confidence_reason: Specific incident report with a named journalist, date of arrest, and a contemporaneous government denial.
ruler_attribution: Strong state nexus through the suspected intelligence-service involvement and the spokesman's response, though direct presidential direction is not shown.
contrary_evidence: The government spokesman denied that the ANR held the journalist.
The source does not establish who physically seized him, only that he disappeared after the arrest.

title: UNHCR gravely concerned by death toll of displaced in DR Congo's east
claim: UNHCR said simultaneous attacks in Ituri left 11 people dead and 250 homes looted and burned, that over 800 deaths from attacks had been recorded in Ituri since February, and that fighting between the Congolese army and M23 displaced more than 160,000 people and created power vacuums in Ituri and North Kivu.
source_confidence_reason: UN humanitarian briefing with concrete casualty and displacement figures and a direct note on government-troop redeployment effects.
ruler_attribution: Mostly indirect: armed groups were the immediate perpetrators, but the report ties worsening civilian risk to the government's inability to hold territory and the security vacuum created by troop redeployment.
contrary_evidence: The immediate attackers were armed groups, not the president personally.
The report notes conflict complexity and multiple militia actors.

title: RDC : 142 personnes tuées et près de 30 000 autres déplacées à la suite des combats dans l'Ouest (HCR)
claim: Radio Okapi reported UNHCR figures that more than 142 people had been killed in the Kwamouth intercommunal violence, about 27,000 people had been displaced, and the Congolese army had been deployed to restore order while the security situation remained tense.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting of a UNHCR briefing with precise figures and the government's security response.
ruler_attribution: Mixed: the violence was intercommunal, but the president was responsible for the state response, including the decision to deploy the army; the report shows response after escalation rather than prevention.
contrary_evidence: The clashes were rooted in local Teke-Yaka disputes over land and customary taxes.
Provincial authorities also set up their own crisis committee and multisector plan.

title: Felix Tshisekedi ordonne la documentation des faits infractionnels commis dans le Grand Bandundu
claim: Radio Okapi reported that Tshisekedi ordered specialized government services to document the offences committed in the Kwamouth conflict in order to speed the restoration of public order in the Grand Bandundu.
source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a presidential council-of-ministers instruction with a clear accountability and order-restoration purpose.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action: this is a ruler-issued instruction to investigate/document violence, though the report does not show completion or results.
contrary_evidence: The report does not show that the documentation led to prosecutions or protection improvements.
The underlying conflict remained active despite the order.

title: RDC : le bilan des manifestations anti-MONUSCO s’alourdit, 15 morts
claim: Radio Okapi reported that the two-day anti-MONUSCO protests had left 15 dead, including three UN peacekeepers and twelve civilians, and that the government said investigations had begun to determine who was responsible.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting of a major protest crackdown with explicit casualty totals and an official note that inquiries had started.
ruler_attribution: Mixed: the protests and deaths involved multiple actors, but the national government was in charge of the security response and publicly acknowledged the need for investigation.
contrary_evidence: Some deaths were of UN peacekeepers rather than protesters.
The source does not identify a single chain of command for each death.
